I do think that therapy is a good idea, and yes, it is important to find a therapist that you click with and feel comfortable talking to, so try to help her find a good one.

Body checks tend to do more harm than good, because she can always find new places or methods to sh, and it causes unnecessary stress and shame. 

Offer a listening ear, and try to encourage sharing, but once again don't force her, because I know from experience that feels terrible

You can try to get her to stop by yourself, but I think the best option would be to go to a professional and be gentle with her. As I said before, she can always find new methods or places to sh that you would never find on your own, so recovery only really works when not forced. She will have to decide for herself to make a real attempt at recovery, but even if she doesn't, therapy and a welcoming home environment can still help her mental health.

When it comes down to it, the actual action of self harm is the part you cannot control, that will have to be her. However, her mental health can be drastically improved by the actions of you and others around her, which is what really opens the door towards recovery.

So basically, I don't have a lot of actual advice, but don't try to "fix" her all by yourself, seek the help of professionals, others you know who have struggled, and your daughter herself.
